summary: The public schedule contains at most ten unique getValue calls, while correctness depends on timer ordering and overlapping asynchronous queries rather than a scalable runtime domain. The implementation queues and resolves each request once.

workload_bound.source_constraint: The calls array contains between zero and ten entries, all with unique keys.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each request is appended once, removed in one batch, mapped to one query key, and resolved once. Across the complete schedule, JavaScript bookkeeping is O(c) time and O(c) pending storage.
Cases cover calls inside, outside, and across consecutive throttle windows; a maximum ten-call burst; query latencies longer than the throttle; and overlapping in-flight batches.
Remote acceptance of the exact native source confirms immediate first dispatch, ordered key-to-value mapping, throttle spacing between query starts, and independence from query completion time.
Every queued request is flushed by the single cooldown timer and every batch result resolves its matching promises; bounded schedules complete without polling, rejection, or a wait cycle.
